BiblicalUsage: Hazar-enan, the village of fountains, stands on the north-east border of Canaan, named in the border law of Numbers and again in Ezekiel's vision of the land divided among the tribes. The same name marks the boundary in the law and in the promise.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the border God drew in the wilderness is the border He keeps in the vision. Hazar-enan is still there when Ezekiel looks ahead, and God's boundaries do not move.
